newsitem.title: USA: WorldCom to build European network.
newsitem.headline: WorldCom to build European network.

text.p: WorldCom Inc on Wednesday said it would build a European fiber optic system to connect its city networks in time for the opening of European Union telecom markets to full competition at the start of 1998.
The first phase, connecting London, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Brussels and Paris, will cost $200 million, it said. That stage is expected to be completed by the end of this year.

WorldCom, the fourth-largest U.S. long-distance carrier, has regulatory approval to build networks and offer national and international services in Britain, the Netherlands, Germany, France and Sweden.

WorldCom, "as an integrated communications services provider, is the telecommunications carrier best positioned to take advantage of the January 1, 1998, deadline," said Colin Williams, chief executive of WorldCom International.

WorldCom will build the rest of its European network in phases, justifying each enlargement as a separate business case. Still, with falling hardware costs, the company expects the entire project would cost less than $1 billion.
At each stage, it will decide whether to offer national telecommunications in addition to the international and city calling and data services supported by the basic network.
WorldCom is already building a trans-Atlantic network called Gemini with Cable and Wireless Plc. That is expected to be operational in February 1998.
WorldCom already has networks in the five cities involved in phase one, plus Stockholm. They came with MFS Communications Co, which WorldCom acquired in a $12.6 billion stock-swap last December.
In building the network, the company will use 2.5 gigabit channels per fiber pair, wave-division multiplexing and optical amplifiers, giving the system a high capacity that can be easily expanded.
As part of the first phase, submarine cables will be laid in the third quarter of the year linking Britain to France and the Netherlands.
